assumptions: Both sides are in-frame coding sequence.
limits: Compares two sequences with each other, so it needs no reference table and makes no claim about an organism's optimum.
bio.jane/contract.noReading: The CUFS distance to each of the record's other genes, which the panel shows as a sorted table; the gene's own codon reading is on codon_usage_analysis.
bio.jane/contract.question: How far is this region's codon usage from the record's other genes (CUFS)?

description: How this region's codon usage compares with the record's OTHER genes (CUFS, Diament, Pinter & Tuller 2014). Every other codon score grades one sequence against a reference TABLE; this one grades two sequences against each other, so it stays available for an organism no authority covers. Answers 'does the gene I inserted use codons like the rest of this construct'.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

feature.description: score this annotated CDS or gene by NAME instead of the selection (the panel's "A CDS / feature…" mode). Its own strand is used unless `reverse` says otherwise.

reverse.description: read the region as the reverse complement. Leave unset to take the strand from the annotation when the selection is exactly an annotated CDS or gene, which is what the panel does.

synonymous.description: normalise each amino acid's codons to sum to 1 (synCUFS), so what remains is the synonymous choice alone. Off compares all 64 codon frequencies, which also reflects amino-acid composition.

name: codon_usage_distance

ceiling.description: the largest distance this run could have produced, for the mode it ran in — read a distance against THIS, never against a constant

furthest.description: the feature whose codon usage is least like the scored region — the odd one out

nearest.description: the feature whose codon usage is closest to the scored region

nearestDistance.description: its distance. 0 would mean an identical codon distribution; the maximum depends on the mode and is reported as `ceiling` beside it — sqrt(2 ln 2) = 1.177 for the plain form, sqrt(2 ln 2 F) = 5.396 for the synonymous one, which normalises each amino acid separately

neighbours.description: every other coding feature with its CUFS distance, nearest first — name, span, codons compared and distance

region.description: what was actually scored, naming the STRAND and where it came from — a reverse-strand gene read forwards is a wrong answer, not a missing one

skipped.description: features that were NOT compared and why — a feature too short for the statistic is reported, never dropped

strandSource.description: `explicit` (you passed `reverse`), `feature` (taken from the annotation the selection matches) or `default` (forwards, nothing said otherwise)

synonymous.description: whether amino-acid composition was normalised away — the same column of figures means a different thing under each
